column1: # ZAP baseline rule configuration: id<TAB>action<TAB>reason (IGNORE, WARN or FAIL)
# The target is served by GitHub Pages, which sets the response headers; a project cannot add
# headers there. Every other rule stays at its default, so a new finding fails the scan.

column3: cache headers are set by GitHub Pages (Cache-Control: max-age=600) and cannot be changed
X-Frame-Options and frame-ancestors are response headers; GitHub Pages sets none and allows no custom ones
X-Content-Type-Options is a response header set by the host, not by the project
reported for the start page, whose source holds none of the debug patterns (checked with grep on site/index.html); caused by the host response
HSTS is set by GitHub Pages for the pages.github.io host; hits on the user-site root, robots.txt and sitemap.xml are 404 pages of the account site, not of this project
CSP is a response header; a meta tag is not evaluated by ZAP and GitHub Pages allows no custom headers
cacheability is decided by the host; the content is public
informational: content comes from the GitHub Pages cache, which is intended for public static files
CSP of the GitHub 404 pages of the account site, not of this project
Permissions-Policy is a response header; GitHub Pages allows no custom headers
GitHub Pages answers every origin with Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *, intended for public static files
Cross-Origin-Embedder/Opener/Resource-Policy are response headers set by the host
